summary:
AgroSpace is a personalized web platform designed to help agricultural workers combat the challenges of climate change. By leveraging critical environmental data—such as temperature, radiation, and rainfall—the project aims to empower farmers to make informed decisions about their crops. The tool focuses on identifying specific agricultural risks and recommending effective crop rotation strategies to optimize water usage and maintain soil health.

Currently developed as a static, user-friendly website using foundational web technologies like HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, the interface allows users to filter recommendations based on their geographic region and specific farming needs. Although the prototype currently operates with built-in local data for its visual charts and guidelines, the ultimate goal is to integrate real-time data directly from NASA satellites, including GPM, Landsat, and MODIS.

Ultimately, this project bridges the gap between advanced satellite technology and everyday farming. It provides a clear, accessible defense mechanism to maximize crop yields and manage pests against a rapidly changing climate, all while respecting and complementing the farmers' invaluable hands-on experience.
details:
• What it does & How it works: The platform gathers environmental data from various NASA satellites (like GPM, Landsat, and MODIS). Through a simple interface, farmers input their regional and agricultural needs, and the system filters this data to provide localized recommendations, crop rotation strategies, and action plans.
  • Benefits: It delivers highly personalized farming advice based on geography, desired crop, soil quality, and rainfall. This helps farmers optimize their water usage and maintain soil health efficiently.
  • Expected Impact: The project aims to provide the agricultural sector with a robust defense mechanism against climate change, soil degradation, and pests, ultimately maximizing crop yields and promoting sustainable farming practices.
  • Tools, Languages & Software Used: The prototype was built as a static website using foundational web technologies: HTML for structure, CSS for design, and JavaScript for interactivity and data filtering. It utilizes Codex, PowerShell, Google Fonts, and PNG files. It intentionally avoids heavy frameworks (like React), servers, or specialized hardware to ensure it runs easily on modern browsers.
  • How the project is creative: It creatively bridges the gap between highly complex aerospace technology and everyday agriculture. Instead of just showing raw data, it translates advanced satellite climate metrics into an accessible, practical, and tailored tool for agricultural workers.
  • Factors the team considered: The team prioritized clarity, ease of access, and regional specificities. Crucially, they designed the platform to empower farmers with informed data without overriding or dismissing their invaluable traditional judgment and hands-on experience.
